Messages.Author: Charles_Bronson
Messages.Body:
Here we go.

I know we have a window to play wake effects to cancel cards "as played". From:

"As played" (a phrase used by many card-canceling effects) comes after the card in question is fully announced and before the played card is replaced and before the effect the play generates. In general, no card or effect can be used in this window. The only ones that can be are the effects that say so, and Wake-style effects that enable such cards to be played ("may play reaction cards" effects, not "untap self" or other effects). [RTR]

So the first sequence is:

1. Tegyrius announce he is playing a Public Trust, and put the card in the table.
and he will play soon after it a deed's the heart desire on a blocking minion.

2. Blocking minion can play a wake effect to play a touch of clarity and cancel the public trust BEFORE the deed's the heart desire enters play.

3. Everyone then replace the 3 cards played.

So far so good.

The new spoiled card, UNLEASHING THE BESTIAL SOUL, says:
only usabe as the action is announced
[dom] choose a minion. the chosen minion cannot play reactions cards this action.
[DOM] as above, and the next reaction card played this action costs +1 blood or life.

So, the question is:

1. A new Salubri announces a bleed with govern. He has Unleashing the bestial soul in hand and will play it as soon as it is possible.

2. Can I play wake on my only tapped minion on the cancel as-played- window with no cancel cards in hand just to "cheat" the cannot play reactions effect from unleashing the bestial soul? and then block the action?

Or can I ONLY play wake effects on this window if I have a cancelling effect?

thanks!
Alexandre Costaa

I am death.
Paul Kersey, Death Wish

Messages.Author: KoRneeshon
Messages.Body:
Because of sequencing rules, you (acting minion) get to play as many effects as you want first (in the specified time window).

BTW, AFAIK there's no wake card that is playable during the "as a card is played" window - these cards are played later. So, if there's a reaction card that allows you to cancel another card as it is played, you cannot play any wakes before it to use it, as opportunity to play a wake shows up later, when the "as a card is played" window is already closed.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> KoRneeshon wrote:
> BTW, AFAIK there's no wake card that is playable during the "as a card is played" window - these cards are played later. So, if there's a reaction card that allows you to cancel another card as it is played, you cannot play any wakes before it to use it, as opportunity to play a wake shows up later, when the "as a card is played" window is already closed.

Wrong, see rulebook:

"ADVANCED RULES

Some effects can cancel a card “as it is played.” These effects, as well as wake effects, are the only effects allowed during the “as played” time period of another card. Even drawing to replace cards, comes after this time period."

Messages.Author: inm8
Messages.Body:
That wake-type cards can be played in the "as it is played" window has been in the rulebook since December 2008 and the rule nor the cards have any implicit or explicit requirement that they have to be tied to another effect... and similar to cancelation effects the wakes played in the "as it is played" window resolve before the effect of the card that is being woken for.

I don´t see anything to be broken, undermining another effect, or limiting design space...if we want to have cards that are not possible to wake to, or cancel it just needs to be written explicitly on the cards´ text

Messages.Author: Čajági
Messages.Body:
Still it is no clear what takes precedense. What exactly means "when it is played" ? It means that i Play blank card and if nobody reacts then text of the card becomes visible ? OR the efect is already there but another vampire can make it blank with playing for. e.g. Iron Heart ?

Acting player plays unleash. The whole card is played (for me that means also the effect). No still in the phase !as it is played" you can play reaction cards that does not go opposite of the wording of the card.

Rules says that "card text takes precedence to the rules". So the card text saying that the target vampire can not play reaction cards should be in effect. (that means the advaced wake rule should not apply) But another vampire can cancel the effect so it never took place. That is how it makes sense to me.

I would really like to see how is the correct order off trigering cards and text in this case.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Čajági wrote:
> Still it is no clear what takes precedense. What exactly means "when it is played" ? It means that i Play blank card and if nobody reacts then text of the card becomes visible ? OR the efect is already there but another vampire can make it blank with playing for. e.g. Iron Heart ?
>
From the rulebook:

> Playing a Card
>
> A card is played by announcing its effects, showing the card and placing it from the hand in the ash heap. Sometimes a card will state to put it into play, you should announce its effects and place the card in the play area.
>
> ADVANCED RULES
>
> Some effects can cancel a card “as it is played.” These effects, as well as wake effects, are the only effects allowed during the “as played” time period of another card. Even drawing to replace cards, comes after this time period.
>
> Čajági wrote:
> Acting player plays unleash. The whole card is played (for me that means also the effect). No still in the phase !as it is played" you can play reaction cards that does not go opposite of the wording of the card.
>
So you play the card, but it can be cancelled before it resolves in the "as it is played" window.
If it isn't cancelled, then you resolve it.
However, as stated by the rulebook, one can play wake cards in that window, before Unleashing the Bestial Soul resolves. And since the wake effects lasts the whole action, that minion will still be under it's effect once the UtBS has resolved.

> Čajági wrote:
> Rules says that "card text takes precedence to the rules". So the card text saying that the target vampire can not play reaction cards should be in effect.
>
Sure, once it has resolved, it will prevent further reaction cards from being played.

>
I would argue that the rules became like that in the first place just to make a couple of cards slightly better, mainly Rewind Time and Terra Incognita, although it does also affect cards like Touch of Clarity etc... That's not that many cards.

In 2004 we got an RTR stopping the "draw a cancel with Barrens" nonsense.
I wouldn't mind having a 2024 RTR stopping the "you can wake to cancel" nonsense TBH.
It is very misleading, as the situation is right now:

You just published a new card that says:
>
> The chosen minion cannot play reaction cards this action.
>
And the first ruling it's gonna get is:
>
> The chosen minion can play a wake as the card is played, before its effects apply.
>
To a fresh player, that's a very unexpected exception, even as aligned as it is with the rulebook.
A change might have to wait for 1.2 revision of the rulebook, and deserve a more careful analysis, but I would also argue for remedying the situation here.
The wake exception in the cancel window is an ugly piece of rule. It's unnecessary, and is just there to make a couple of cards slightly better. Simplifying and removing it sounds sensible.

Messages.Author: KoRneeshon
Messages.Body:
I think it's getting much clearer when you realize that "Action card is played" is a separate step before "Action is announced" step. Wakes can be played in the "as card is played" window, and "as the action is announced" cards are, well, self-explanatory.
I agree it weakens few action mods, but cannot deny it is logical and not that hard to understand.
